This reminds me of the Ikigai chart. 

Ikigai is basically a Japanese concept of the meaning of someone’s life. The chart helps you find a sense of purpose in life, as well as being a source of motivation. 

According to a study by Michiko Kumano, feeling ikigai as described in Japanese is usually the sense of
accomplishment and fulfillment that follows when people pursue their passions.

The Ikigai chart is a similar Venn diagram but with four circles representing: what you are good at, What You Love, what the world needs, and what you can be paid for.

What you love and are good at create your passion. What you love and what the world needs is a mission. What the World needs and what you get paid for are your vocation or calling. And finally, what you get paid for and What Your good at make your profession.

So it’s the intersection of four things: passion, mission, vocation (calling), and profession that creates a sense of ikigai.

The idea is you want to find something your passionate about, something that can have positive impact on the world (mission), something you feel called to, and something you can get paid to do. That’s your Ikigai
